decisions.reason: Because A extends the core airfield-control line, was publicly promoted as a new industry standard, and any weaker airport demand can still be framed as temporary, management is likely to stay committed.

Because C supports the installed base and service business but carries less sunk R&D and less public commitment than the main technology platforms, management keeps it while seeing a moderate withdrawal risk.

Because D is closely linked to the established airfield-lighting offer yet is a relatively narrow, low-visibility training product, management keeps it for now but would drop it sooner than a core system if resources tighten.

Because E fits the announced move toward integrated, collaborative and data-driven airport operations and likely required meaningful software-development effort, management is inclined to justify continued support.
Because F was presented as an advanced flagship surveillance product central to the firm's future direction, its high visibility and sunk development costs strongly favor continued commitment.
